name: Solar Panel

claims.claim_text: Every panel datasheet rates output at a nominal 1000 watts per square metre of incident sunlight, which makes the industry standard easy to hold in your head and makes any panel's rating directly comparable with any other's.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you've got a 400 watt solar panel, that's at a nominal one, 1000 watts per square meter
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Peak output does not come on the hottest day: a clear cold winter day with slight haze can beat midsummer, because the haze scatters light onto the panel from more directions while the cold keeps the cells efficient.
claims.quote_verbatim: your peak power is going to be put out here in Cleveland in the middle of winter on a nice clear day
claims.speaker: Martin Lorton
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Martin Lorton - Variegated Video Vagility

claims.claim_text: Panels run more efficiently cold, enough that installations in hot climates drip water over the array to cool it, powering the pump from the array's own output and still coming out ahead.
claims.quote_verbatim: they actually drip feed water over them to actually cool down the solar panels, makes them more efficient
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Wearables Might Have Limited Fashion Options - Lachrymogenic Lane Language

claims.claim_text: Laying a panel flat rather than angling it at the sun costs twenty to thirty percent before anything else, and a flat installation compounds that with losses in any covering glass and with the lack of airflow behind the panel, which raises its temperature and lowers efficiency again.
claims.quote_verbatim: you lose like 20, 30% just from it being flat instead of angled
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Wearables Might Have Limited Fashion Options - Lachrymogenic Lane Language

claims.claim_text: A single panel produces roughly forty volts, so a string inverter system wires them in series — twelve panels giving something like 460 volts open circuit — which is why a domestic roof is carrying several hundred volts of DC.
claims.quote_verbatim: a regular solar panel is about 40 odd volts, something like that. So you put them in series
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Four ordinary panels in series reach about 160 volts, and shorting a string at that voltage sustains a DC arc: unlike a low-voltage short, the plasma keeps burning once struck and can be pulled apart while still conducting, which is what makes rooftop DC wiring dangerous in a way a battery of the same energy is not.
claims.quote_verbatim: they got four solar panels, just regular solar panels. I think they're 40 volts each or something like that, right? So about 160 volts
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Deliberately fitting an inverter smaller than the panel it serves — 290 watts of inverter on a 370 watt panel — costs very little because the panel only reaches its rating for perhaps half an hour a day. The design has to be judged on energy over the year, not on peak power.
claims.quote_verbatim: 290 watt inverters on a 370 watt panel
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Roof aspect dominates nameplate rating: a three kilowatt array relocated to a poorly oriented face of the roof delivered about one kilowatt at best in winter, a third of what the same hardware produced before it was moved.
claims.quote_verbatim: a 3 kilowatt system. The best I've seen out of that so far is like 1 kilowatt
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Relocating an existing array to a suboptimal aspect is still worth doing once the original system has paid for itself, because the marginal cost is a few hundred dollars of labour and the alternative is scrapping working hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: might get half the, half the energy out of it that I used to because it's on the other side of the roof, but who cares? Right. It's already paid for itself
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Roof suitability can be assessed before anyone visits, using tools that model usable roof area together with tree shading from a three-dimensional model — which will sometimes rule a site out immediately.
claims.quote_verbatim: it'll map how much energy square area your roof is and tell you how much your solar energy and it'll show shading for trees
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Panels are rectangles and a roof cut into many small triangular faces cannot take them efficiently, so roof geometry rather than roof area is often what limits an installation.
claims.quote_verbatim: solar panels are square. And your roof is triangular
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A three kilowatt system of twelve panels falls well short of covering a house; at around 250 watts per panel it takes twenty or more before an array meaningfully offsets household consumption.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got to have like 20 plus panels or something before you even start getting serious
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A panel is roughly 1.8 metres by 1 metre, which is the figure to measure a roof against when working out how many will physically fit before asking what they will generate.
claims.quote_verbatim: the panels are about 1.8 meters by one meter
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A well-sited array reaches slightly over its datasheet rating on a very good day with high insolation, so the nameplate figure is a realistic peak rather than an optimistic one.
claims.quote_verbatim: the system based on the data sheet is rated at three kilowatts. And I think I get actually slightly over that on a really good day
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Solar Factories and HVDC Lines - Pollent Power Pushing

claims.claim_text: Installers guarantee an annual energy figure rather than a power figure, and a first measured year came in at 5.26 megawatt hours against a 4.8 megawatt hour guarantee — the guarantee being conservative by roughly ten percent.
claims.quote_verbatim: they guaranteed 4.8 megawatt hours of energy off of this panel. And it turns out I got 5.26 megawatt hours
claims.speaker: Bob Simpson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Simpson - Ardent Automotive Artisan

claims.claim_text: A cloudless day should produce a smooth generation curve, so dips in that curve are diagnostic. Comparing the same day across two arrays on the same roof separates a real fault from weather, because genuine cloud shows up on both.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you've ever seen like the solar curve on a perfect cloudless day, it's just this smooth
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Because a string is wired in series, a single degraded panel is bypassed and can pull down the output of the whole string — which is why physical handling damage during installation, producing microcracks invisible from the ground, shows up as a system-level shortfall.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're all in series, right? It's a big series string of 12 panels. If one of them goes bad, it, it will get bypassed
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Converting an existing string installation to per-panel microinverters costs more than the old panels are worth, so the high-voltage DC string stays even where the owner would prefer not to have it — the retrofit economics, not the safety argument, decide it.
claims.quote_verbatim: buying a microinverter for each one of my existing old panels is like cost, cost more than the panels are worth
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A whole-house monitor that works by differencing imported against exported power cannot resolve small loads while the array is generating, because the differential is large. Measuring at night, with generation at zero, recovers an extra digit of resolution and makes circuit-by-circuit measurement possible.
claims.quote_verbatim: waited until night when my solar panels weren't producing anything
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A long DC run from a detached structure back to the inverter carries a real voltage drop, and it is not something the installer surveying cable routes will necessarily raise — the conduit and the electrical consequence are usually different people's expertise.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's probably a pretty significant drop through the the cables
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Like a steam engine in your house

claims.claim_text: A grid-tied inverter is two stages: the panel string feeds a boost or buck-boost converter that establishes a four to five hundred volt DC bus, and an H-bridge then chops that bus into a sine wave synchronised to the grid.
claims.quote_verbatim: the solar panels go directly into a boost converter
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Unused generation is not a problem to dispose of: with no current drawn, panels simply sit at their open-circuit voltage and produce nothing, so curtailment costs nothing but the energy foregone.
claims.quote_verbatim: the energy from the solar panels doesn't have to go anywhere
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Regions that installed solar earliest have the least controllable fleet: the great majority of those inverters have no connectivity at all, so the capacity cannot be curtailed remotely no matter what the grid needs.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're all dumb inverters. They weren't connected
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Whether a load is running on local generation is settled by where it sits relative to the meter and by which way current flows: with the charger wired ahead of the metering point and no import registering, the energy demonstrably came from the panels rather than the grid.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's all done before the metering
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A modest battery is enough to bridge the evening demand peak: with generation stopping around midday for a west-facing array, storage carried the house through to eight or nine at night before any grid import resumed — covering the whole dip in the daily demand curve.
claims.quote_verbatim: usually stop using power around noon, given where my panels are. And I don't start using power again from the grid till, like, 8 or 9 p.m
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Managing demand in a constrained neighbourhood proved cheaper than building a substation to serve it, and the comparison is worse than it first looks for the substation: it produces nothing once built, where distributed generation keeps producing energy for its whole life.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was a lot cheaper than building a new substation
claims.speaker: Ari Gerstman
claims.episode_title: Renewable Energy Policy with Ari Gerstman

claims.claim_text: Utilities demand extensive telemetry from distributed generation and raise security objections that are not unreasonable — simultaneous remote shutdown of an entire district's generation on a sunny day would be a genuine grid event — and the realistic attack surface is the inverter rather than the panel.
claims.quote_verbatim: somebody hacked into every single solar panel in the district and shut it down
claims.speaker: Ari Gerstman
claims.episode_title: Renewable Energy Policy with Ari Gerstman

claims.claim_text: The claim that a country's entire demand fits on a small area of panels is arithmetically defensible and practically empty, because it sets aside both storage and the transmission needed to move that power from where it is generated to where it is used.
claims.quote_verbatim: technically in theory, you can power like an entire country with, you know, just like a small, relatively small amount of solar panels
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Covering irrigation canals with panels pays twice: the structure anchors to solid ground either side of a channel only a few metres wide, the shade suppresses evaporation, and unlike open water there is no bird fouling. Floating arrays on lakes get the cooling benefit but bring the problem that floating structures move and collide.
claims.quote_verbatim: they've covered their water canals with solar panels
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Given finite roof area, photovoltaic panels beat solar hot water because electricity is fungible: it can heat water through a heat pump, charge a vehicle, run the house or go into storage, where a solar thermal collector only ever produces hot water.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're better off devoting your roof space to solar panels
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Road-surface photovoltaics are far more expensive than rooftop for a fraction of the energy once the concrete, glass and structure are counted. Mounting angled panels above a path instead — as a canopy — keeps the conventional geometry and gains weather protection underneath.
claims.quote_verbatim: these things are massively more expensive than rooftop solar
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Wearables Might Have Limited Fashion Options - Lachrymogenic Lane Language

claims.claim_text: Putting an existing panel under glass in a novel location is packaging rather than innovation in solar technology, and the distinction matters when judging what a project actually claims to have advanced.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're doing is taking existing solar panels and whacking them under some glass on the road
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Worktrips and Workspaces - Junket Jactation Jiltedness

claims.claim_text: Cells optimised for indoor light are a distinct product from rooftop panels, and they are what makes a genuinely battery-free indoor sensor possible.
claims.quote_verbatim: it has a solar panel on it that is really efficient, uh, indoors
claims.speaker: Richard Ginus

claims.claim_text: Eight hundred watts of vehicle-mounted panel puts very little energy into a car battery over a day — enough that continuous driving is impossible even under full sun in the Australian outback, and recharging means stopping for hours and clearing the panels.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's only got 800 Watts worth of solar panels
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A vehicle's integrated solar roof realistically adds around five miles of range a day, which is meaningful for some owners and negligible for others — and a power pole or tree shading the parking spot removes even that.
claims.quote_verbatim: it might give you an extra five miles a day maybe
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The argument for a solar roof on an electric vehicle is not daily range but never being completely stranded: a slow trickle turns being stuck permanently into being stuck for a day.
claims.quote_verbatim: think every EV should have, like, at least a solar roof on it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Spacecraft solar panels are built as cells assembled onto a printed circuit board backing, and deployment is done with a spring that pushes the panel or antenna element out once released.
claims.quote_verbatim: we have a printer circuit board backing that we assemble those cells onto
claims.speaker: Dan Esparon
claims.episode_title: Satellite Design Engineering with Dan Esparon

claims.claim_text: A lander found intact on Mars years later had soft-landed successfully and deployed four of its five panels; the one that stayed shut was covering the antenna that would have phoned home. Stacking a communications dependency underneath a deployable is a single point of failure that no amount of redundancy elsewhere covers.
claims.quote_verbatim: it deployed four of its five solar panels
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Glass and Gongkai GSM - Unzymotic Ursidae Upbuilding

claims.claim_text: A satellite lost in 1967 resumed transmitting 46 years later, when its tumble happened to bring the panels into enough light and the antenna into the right orientation — a reminder that photovoltaics have no wear-out mechanism in the way that chemistry and mechanisms do.
claims.quote_verbatim: 46 years, it started transmitting again
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Externally mounted spacecraft panels swing between about minus 100 and plus 100 degrees Celsius, but the cold extreme is benign because no current is being drawn from them there — the thermal cycling matters more than either absolute limit.
claims.quote_verbatim: they'll see, you know, negative 100 C to positive 100 C
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Shaun Meehan - Doctiloquent Dove Deployer

claims.claim_text: A domestic battery-and-solar installation arrives as half a dozen separate sheet-metal boxes that have to be conduited together, commissioned and tied into the panel, and the electrician's time frequently costs more than the hardware itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: you often end up spending more money on electrician time installing it
claims.speaker: Kerry Scharfglass

claims.claim_text: The quality spread in both panels and inverters is wide enough to matter over a twenty-year life, and the arithmetic makes it concrete: one percent of a three kilowatt system is thirty watts being turned into heat continuously, every hour the sun is up.
claims.quote_verbatim: a big difference in quality between, you know, you're sort of $300 inverter and your $2,000 inverter
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Solar Factories and HVDC Lines - Pollent Power Pushing

claims.claim_text: A premium domestic installation paid back in about five years against panels warranted for twenty years of output and an inverter warranted for ten, which is what makes the economics work even without a generous feed-in tariff.
claims.quote_verbatim: would pay back in five years tops
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Solar, FPGAs and Maxim Integrated - Solar Shopper Sickness

claims.claim_text: Solar projects in low-income markets fail on financing rather than on hardware: microfinance interest rates are high because borrowers commit and then default, and recovering the equipment is expensive enough that the cost feeds back into the rates. Retaining ownership and profit-sharing with a local operator sidesteps the credit problem entirely.
claims.quote_verbatim: solar panels are not particularly costly to to purchase but there are a lot of failed solar panel projects
claims.speaker: Stefan Dzisiewski-Smith

claims.claim_text: A 12 kilowatt array of twenty to twenty-eight panels plus battery storage and installation came to about thirty-two thousand dollars before incentives, against which a thirty percent federal credit and a utility programme payment covered roughly nineteen thousand.
claims.quote_verbatim: that is a boatload of money no doubt there's a 30 percent federal tax credit
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Like a steam engine in your house

claims.claim_text: An order-of-magnitude feel for energy per unit panel area and per unit battery mass lets an engineer reject an implausible product claim on sight, without doing the calculation — and the calculation is then worth doing to confirm the instinct rather than to form it.
claims.quote_verbatim: we can you know get charge a battery with this solar panel and I'm going no you can't look at the size of it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Glass and Gongkai GSM - Unzymotic Ursidae Upbuilding

claims.claim_text: The recurring claim that the eighty percent a panel does not convert can be mirrored into a second panel, and again into a third, to exceed a hundred percent efficiency is a perpetual motion argument in new packaging — the unconverted energy is not sitting there as reflected light waiting to be collected.
claims.quote_verbatim: if we use mirrors and then we just reflect that re reflect that back into another solar panel
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Hundreds of hours went into optimising a half-watt panel and battery chemistry to sustain readings every minute, and users turned out to be delighted with four readings a day — a thousandth of the power budget. A few hours of asking users first would have removed the entire engineering problem.
claims.quote_verbatim: turns out like nobody cares. If you send readings four times a day, people are thrilled
claims.speaker: Luke Iseman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Iseman of yCombinator

claims.claim_text: Maximum power point tracking is an algorithm rather than a component: measure the panel's voltage and current, step the presented input impedance, and keep stepping until the output passes over the peak of the power curve — then repeat as the sun moves, because the peak moves with it.
claims.quote_verbatim: you basically excite the solar cell and then you kind of back off and you see what it does
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A charger listed as supporting maximum power point tracking may only mean an application note exists describing how to implement it externally with a microcontroller; dedicated parts that do it internally are a different class of device, and the distributor's parametric field does not distinguish them.
claims.quote_verbatim: it had, it had said MPPT in like the, the digi key thing
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

attribution_notes: attribution_reliable was not trusted. ep540 labels both speakers as Fran Blanche; the passage describing Australian feed-in tariffs and national uptake is unambiguously Dave Jones and was not attributed to the guest. No claim from that episode is included.
ep206 (Martin Lorton), ep630 (Ari Gerstman) and ep309 label host questions with the guest's name; only material unambiguously the guest's own was used.
ep220 labels the satellite guest's thermal description as 'Dave Jones'; the speaker could not be resolved with confidence, so that claim carries speaker: null.

Feed-in tariff politics, subsidy-driven purchase decisions, individual household bills and product-fire anecdotes were excluded as reception and local policy rather than transferable engineering knowledge.
